chunks.text:
Venlafaxine is used in adults to treat major depressive disorder.
Venlafaxine extended-release capsules are used to treat generalized anxiety disorder.
Generalized anxiety disorder is excessive worrying that is difficult to control.
Venlafaxine extended-release capsules are also used to treat social anxiety disorder.
Social anxiety disorder is extreme fear of interacting with others or performing in front of others that interferes with normal life.
Venlafaxine extended-release capsules are also used to treat panic disorder.
Panic disorder is sudden, unexpected attacks of extreme fear and worry about these attacks.
Venlafaxine belongs to a class of medications called selective serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs).
Venlafaxine works by increasing the amounts of serotonin and norepinephrine.
Serotonin and norepinephrine are natural substances in the brain.
These substances help maintain mental balance.

Some young people may have increased suicidal thoughts when first starting a medicine to treat depression.
Stay alert to changes in your mood or symptoms.
Your family or caregivers should also watch for sudden changes in your behavior.
Taking this medicine during pregnancy could harm the baby.
Taking venlafaxine in the month before delivery may increase your risk of severe bleeding after childbirth.
However, stopping venlafaxine may not be safe for you.
Do not start or stop venlafaxine without asking your doctor.
If you are pregnant, your name may be listed on a pregnancy registry.
The registry is used to track the effects of venlafaxine on the baby.
Ask a doctor if it is safe to breastfeed while using venlafaxine.

chunks.text:
Take venlafaxine as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Take with food at the same time each day.
Swallow the extended-release capsule or tablet whole.
Do not crush, chew, break, or open it.
If you cannot swallow a capsule whole, open it and mix the medicine with applesauce.
Swallow the mixture right away without chewing.
Tell your doctor if you have any changes in sexual function.
Such changes include loss of interest in sex.
Such changes include trouble having an orgasm.
Such changes include problems with erections or ejaculation in men.
Some sexual problems can be treated.
Your symptoms may not improve for up to several weeks.
Do not stop using venlafaxine suddenly.
You could have severe and long-lasting unpleasant symptoms.
These symptoms include agitation, confusion, tingling or electric shock feelings, aggression, violent behavior, suicidal thoughts, vision changes, or increased blood pressure.

chunks.text:
Do not drink alcohol.
Ask your doctor before taking a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) such as aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, Advil, Aleve, Motrin, and others.

Avoid driving or hazardous activity until you know how venlafaxine will affect you.
Your reactions could be impaired.
